reason: The dominant failure signature is that the FIFO's status flags do not track the occupancy count as required by the specification: full stays 0 when the FIFO is full (@85 ns), empty stays 1 when data is present (@125 ns), and almost_full stays 0 when the AF_LEVEL threshold is crossed (@210 ns). These stale/late flags then cause the downstream protocol violations (write when full @355 ns, read when empty @420 ns) and the simultaneous read/write data mismatch @350 ns. Structural RTL analysis confirms a reset-coverage defect: 'fifo_count' is written in the sequential block at projects/fifo/rtl/sync_fifo.sv:63 but is not assigned in the reset clause, so occupancy (and hence every flag derived from it) starts from an indeterminate/uninitialized value and remains permanently skewed relative to the actual pointer difference (rd_ptr/wr_ptr are reset at line 43). This is a violation of REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-011 and REQ-012 by the design → Decision Rule Case 6/7/8 (RTL violates spec, uninitialized state, protocol protection not implemented correctly).
category: Functional / Reset Initialization → Status-Flag & Protocol Violation
spec_reference: REQ-007 (full), REQ-008 (empty), REQ-009 (almost_full/AF_LEVEL), REQ-011 (overflow), REQ-012 (underflow), REQ-013 (wr_count); Reset Behavior section: 'reset (low, asynchronous) resets ...'
log_reference: @85 ns Full flag mismatch (exp 1, got 0); @125 ns Empty flag mismatch (exp 0, got 1); @210 ns Almost full flag mismatch (exp 1, got 0); @350 ns data mismatch on simultaneous rd/wr; @355 ns write while full; @420 ns read while empty
rtl_reference: projects/fifo/rtl/sync_fifo.sv:63 (always block writing almost_empty, almost_full, empty, fifo_count, full, overflow, underflow — fifo_count missing from reset clause); also sv:43 (pointer reset), sv:54 (memory block, no reset)
tb_reference: Scoreboard source not provided; one anomalous check message '@85 ns FIFO count mismatch: Expected 15, Got 15' suggests a possible comparison/reporting defect in the count checker that should be reviewed separately
recommended_fix: 1) In the reset branch of the always block at sync_fifo.sv:63, initialize fifo_count <= '0 (along with full, empty, almost_full, almost_empty, overflow, underflow) so occupancy is deterministic after the asynchronous active-low reset. 2) Derive full/empty/almost_full/almost_empty from the next-state count (fifo_count_next computed from wr_en & ~full and rd_en & ~empty in the same cycle) or make them combinational functions of fifo_count so they assert on the cycle the threshold is reached rather than one cycle late. 3) Ensure the simultaneous read/write case keeps fifo_count unchanged while still forwarding/advancing both pointers, which fixes the @350 ns data mismatch. 4) Gate the write/read strobes with the corrected full/empty flags and pulse overflow/underflow for exactly one cycle per REQ-011/REQ-012. 5) Separately, audit the scoreboard count-compare that reported 'Expected 15, Got 15' (likely wrong field printed or wrong operator) — this is a TB reporting issue layered on top of the RTL defect.

evidence.description: Sequential block drives fifo_count and all status flags but fifo_count is absent from the reset clause, leaving occupancy uninitialized after reset (Case 7 style X/indeterminate state).
evidence.snippet: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin if (!rst_n) begin full<=0; empty<=1; ... /* fifo_count NOT reset */ end else ... end

evidence.description: wr_ptr/rd_ptr ARE reset, so pointer-based occupancy and the separately maintained fifo_count can diverge immediately after reset, producing permanently wrong flags.

Three independent flag checks (full, empty, almost_full) all fail in the same direction: the flag lags/does not reflect actual occupancy — a systematic count/threshold defect, not a random data corruption.

Overflow (write when full) and underflow (read when empty) protection failed, i.e. REQ-011/REQ-012 protection mechanisms are ineffective because they depend on the broken full/empty flags → Case 8 protocol implemented incorrectly in RTL.

Spec unambiguously requires full when no space remains, empty when no data available, almost_full at AF_LEVEL, and one-cycle overflow/underflow pulses. No self-contradiction exists in the requirement set, so Case 9 (Spec Bug) is excluded.
Concurrent read/write handling corrupts dout/count bookkeeping — a classic symptom of incorrect count update for the simultaneous case in the same block at line 63.

evidence.reference: Scoreboard: 'No scoreboard found' in collected artifacts
evidence.description: TB predictor source unavailable, so a scoreboard off-by-one cannot be fully excluded; the '@85 ns Expected 15, Got 15' message is the only TB-side anomaly and affects a single check, not the flag failures.

reasoning_chain.observation: Seven errors: three status-flag mismatches, one data mismatch on simultaneous rd/wr, and two protocol-protection violations (write-when-full, read-when-empty).
reasoning_chain.inference: Failures cluster around occupancy tracking and flag generation rather than data path storage.

reasoning_chain.observation: Spec REQ-007..REQ-013 define full/empty/almost_full/almost_empty/overflow/underflow/count behavior consistently; no contradictory statements.
RTL structural analysis: fifo_count is written in the always block at line 63 but is missing from that block's reset clause; pointers at line 43 are reset.
reasoning_chain.inference: Post-reset occupancy is indeterminate; all flags derived from fifo_count are wrong from time 0 — an RTL initialization defect (Case 7) and a spec violation (Case 6).

reasoning_chain.observation: full=0 at the moment the scoreboard expects full=1, and empty=1 when data should be readable; almost_full never asserts at threshold.
reasoning_chain.inference: Flags are computed from a stale/registered count instead of the next-state count, so threshold crossings are missed or delayed — consistent with the reset/count defect.

reasoning_chain.observation: Overflow/underflow guard errors occur AFTER the flag errors (355 ns, 420 ns).
reasoning_chain.inference: Protocol violations are downstream consequences of the broken flags, confirming a single RTL root cause (Case 8) rather than bad stimulus; a driver bug would not also corrupt full/empty flag values reported by the DUT.

reasoning_chain.observation: One log line reports 'FIFO count mismatch: Expected 15, Got 15' where expected == actual, and scoreboard source was not collected.
reasoning_chain.inference: There is a secondary TB reporting/compare defect worth fixing, but it does not explain the DUT flag values; it lowers confidence modestly rather than changing the classification.

reasoning_chain.observation: Driver and monitor artifacts show no reported protocol/sampling anomalies, and deterministic pre-analysis independently suggests RTL Bug with a reset-coverage finding.
reasoning_chain.inference: Cases 1–5 (TB Bug paths) are not supported by evidence; final classification is RTL Bug.

missing_artifacts: Full RTL source of sync_fifo.sv (lines 30–110) to confirm exact flag equations and the reset clause contents

DUT parameter values used in this test (DATA_WIDTH, DEPTH/ADDR_WIDTH, AF_LEVEL, AE_LEVEL, FWFT vs standard mode)
Waveform (VCD/FSDB) around 80–130 ns showing rst_n, wr_en, rd_en, fifo_count, full, empty
Monitor sampling code / clocking block to confirm flags are sampled on the correct clock edge

alternative_hypotheses.reason: The '@85 ns FIFO count mismatch: Expected 15, Got 15' check fails with identical expected and actual values, and an off-by-one in the reference model (asserting full at count 15 for a depth-16 FIFO) could also explain the full/almost_full mismatches. Scoreboard source was not available to disprove this; if the reference model is wrong, this becomes Case 3.

Flags sampled one cycle early (wrong clocking-block skew) would produce exactly this 'flag is late' pattern for full/empty/almost_full. However it would not explain the write-when-full and read-when-empty protocol violations, which imply the DUT itself did not block the transfers.

If neither the full RTL flag equations nor the scoreboard model can be obtained, evidence would be limited to structural hints; current reset-coverage finding plus consistent multi-flag failure pattern is sufficient to avoid this outcome.
